- If sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤ 0.33) or neutral (0.00), model often underestimates downside risk; add downward buffer or adjust for volatility clustering.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior day), model frequently overcorrects and overshoots; apply dampening factor or lagged momentum correction.
- When true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., after 70+ peak, price drops to 65–68), model often fails to recognize it; adjust for recent high volatility or sentiment reversal.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to misalign horizon (e.g., 30d forecast too flat when sentiment is volatile); use sentiment-weighted smoothing or adaptive horizon decay.
- Model consistently underestimates true price drops after sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish; add penalty for sentiment reversal in forecast adjustment.
